- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward momentum reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a drop; apply a lagged correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast 2–3 periods after spike.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; increase forecast slope gradually over next 3–5 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per period until convergence; if below, increase by 1–3%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early periods (1–5) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 3 periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral), model often fails to capture sentiment drift; treat as “low signal” and apply 1–2% bias toward historical mean.
